purpose: Held-out evidence review; fictional. Review-only. Never provide to the generating model.
material_findings: Both cabinets have genuine signed buyer acceptance: A on 6 October and B on 23 October. Delivery of B on 20 October is distinct. A minor label issue did not prevent acceptance and was corrected. A claim that no acceptance or no payment obligation exists contradicts the packet.

The contract price 22500 less cleared deposit 7500, cleared part payment 2750 and bilateral price credit 1750 leaves 10500 outstanding. The credit and part payment apply to cabinet A, leaving A 3000 and B 7500. Demand acknowledges these items; do not invent a payment contradiction.

Storage was requested in writing by the authorized buyer, approved under clause 3, documented at genuine third-party cost (five times 130 equals 650), paid by Supplier and passed through without markup. Buyer confirmed both receipt and matching amount. No missing-extra-approval defense is supported.

Total open balance 11150 is supported as an outstanding amount, distinct from the amount presently overdue. The complete project account has no unidentified earlier credit or reversed payment. Do not invent reconciliation uncertainty merely from other cases.

A original payment date was 20 October, fourteen days after 6 October acceptance, but authorized representatives agreed in writing on 19 October to extend it to 4 November. The accounting system explicitly retains a stale field. The 22 October part payment does not revoke the extension.

B 7500 is payable 6 November, fourteen calendar days after 23 October acceptance. Storage 650 is payable 10 November, fourteen calendar days after confirmed receipt of both invoices on 27 October. On 30 October no documented instalment is overdue under those terms.

The contract rejects automatic acceleration and the demand supplies no further acceleration agreement. Distinguish the genuine debt evidence from the unsupported assertion that all 11150 is immediately payable on default or by 2 November. No external legal conclusion is required.

Demand receipt on 30 October at 10:10 is affirmatively acknowledged. Do not call receipt unknown. 2 November is an asserted supplier deadline; it is not established as a court or statutory date. Practical verification should focus on confirming the extension remains operative and any later modification, account update, and planned payment handling without sending a reply or calendar change.
verification_rationale: Use the four documents together: signed acceptance and storage authorization are adverse evidence that support real obligations; the credit and part payment reconcile the demand rather than refute it. The material dispute concerns when supported balances are payable and the supplier reliance on a stale system due date. A good review distinguishes outstanding, currently due, overdue and demanded amounts, preserves confirmed receipt and avoids importing absent-acceptance, unapproved-extra or unknown-payment assumptions from other fixtures.
